s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of bilateral lower limb redness, pain, and swelling with sclerotic plaques in a patient undergoing chemotherapy
salient_findings: Acute onset of redness, pain, and swelling of both lower limbs
Ill-defined, erythematoedematous plaques symmetrically distributed along the shins
key_facts: Patient is a man in his late 70s
Received 4 cycles of chemotherapy with carboplatin, pemetrexed, and pembrolizumab
Currently in maintenance with pemetrexed-pembrolizumab
Edema appeared 5 days after the patient's 8th cycle of chemotherapy
Patient remained afebrile and systemically well
No elevation of inflammatory markers
Normal kidney, liver, and heart functions
Venous Doppler ultrasonography of legs showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis
Pathology showed thickened dermal collagen with activated fibroblasts and lymphocytic perivascular infiltration

shortlist.label: Erythema nodosum
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of redness, pain, and swelling of lower limbs with sclerotic plaques

shortlist.label: Chemotherapy-induced scleroderma-like reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient received chemotherapy and developed sclerotic plaques

shortlist.label: Pemetrexed-induced scleroderma-like reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was on maintenance with pemetrexed-pembrolizumab when symptoms appeared

shortlist.label: Erythema induratum
shortlist.why_kept: Symmetrically distributed erythematoedematous plaques with induration on lower limbs

shortlist.label: Scleredema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed sclerotic plaques and had a history of chemotherapy

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of redness, pain, and swelling of both lower limbs, which evolved into sclerotic plaques, appeared 5 days after the 8th cycle of chemotherapy with pemetrexed, and the pathology showed thickened dermal collagen with activated fibroblasts, consistent with a scleroderma-like reaction

rejected.label: Erythema nodosum
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic nodules and no evidence of systemic inflammation

rejected.label: Chemotherapy-induced scleroderma-like reaction
rejected.why: While possible, the specific temporal relationship with pemetrexed administration makes Pemetrexed-induced scleroderma-like reaction more likely

rejected.label: Erythema induratum
rejected.why: Typically presents with recurrent nodules on the calves, which is not consistent with the patient's symmetric, ill-defined plaques

rejected.label: Scleredema
rejected.why: Usually associated with diabetes or infections, which are not mentioned in the case, and the pathology does not match
